main_text.l: Ars bona vi magna non est mercabilis auri,Illa sed in pigro parta labore venit.

l.i: LAurentio debetur merito laurea, Huc ergo Scheichi, & hinc tuam fer lauream, Ex Gratiarum pratuli intonsa coma Aptam: probis, & his unis, quos auream Natura docuit ipsa temperantiam, Fas carpere illinc: improbis autem nefas. At tu fuscae Scheichi vinculum comae Amicè suscipe, quod pia dextra porrigit.

main_text.l: UBi malignus nodus est, Quaerendus asper cuneus est: Nam cunei vis est maxima. Ingenium si sit plumbeum, Ut haereat fixissimis Radicibus scientia Animo tandem, unus cuneus est, Et alter, Diligentia, Et continuata Motio Cerebri, & crebra lectio. His, AEgidi, cuneis tibi Adeptus es hanc lauream. Sic perge, habebis auream.
HUc ades, ursinum qui praefers nomine robur, Hac tegat ornatum laurus odora caput. Laurea frontis honos, tali quae Jaspide fulget, Cum natura usus perficit artis opus.

page.notes: The second line of the opening couplet reads "im pigro" in the scan; this is most likely "in" and is kept as the letters appear. The poet's name in XVII is read as "Breslerus" and is uncertain. The stanzas are printed in verse lines with broken lines marked by line breaks. The heading lines are printed in larger roman type and are treated as level 3 headings. The initial letters L, U and H are large woodcut initials and are joined to the first word.
